## Code that runs

Chunks execute at render time. `echo: true` shows the code; without it only the output
appears (the project default). Seed every random draw so the projected numbers are the
numbers students find in the chapter.

```{python}
#| echo: true
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
print(rng.binomial(n=80, p=0.65, size=5))
```

## A figure from code

```{python}
#| fig-align: center
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
draws = rng.binomial(80, 0.65, size=2000) / 80
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3.6))
ax.hist(draws, bins=np.arange(0.4, 0.9, 0.02), histtype="step", lw=2.5, color="#eb6834")
ax.axvline(0.65, color="#52514e", ls=":", lw=2)
ax.set_xlabel("observed fraction"); ax.set_ylabel("runs")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

## Code here, output on the next slide

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide
for n in (20, 80, 320):
    print(f"{n:>4} reads: sd of the fraction ≈ {np.sqrt(0.65 * 0.35 / n):.3f}")
```

## An illustration drawn from text

Graphviz (`{dot}`) and Mermaid (`{mermaid}`) blocks render as diagrams; no image file to keep in sync.

```{dot}
//| fig-width: 7
digraph G {
  rankdir=LR; node [shape=box, fontname="Helvetica", style=rounded];
  truth [label="a truth you chose\n(m = 0.65)"];
  world [label="the process, as code"];
  data  [label="data (49 of 80)"];
  answer [label="an estimate — and how far it wanders"];
  truth -> world -> data -> answer;
}
```

## Speaker notes

Write notes in a `.notes` block under any slide. They are **removed from the public build**
and kept in the instructor build (`tools/build_slides.sh --instructor`), where `s` opens them.

::: {.notes}
Only you see this, and only in the instructor build.
:::

## Headings are a public interface

Run-sheets in the instructor repo cite slides **by heading text**, not by number. Adding or
reordering slides is free; renaming a heading means updating that week's run-sheet.
